detectionVerification.result: PASS for edge and yandex on this machine; chrome not yet checked
detectionVerification.method: Not a contrived test. The user reinstalled both extensions rather than reloading them, which wiped `browser.storage.local` — the new installation ids prove it (edge 56024a43 -> 5507a07a, yandex 0bcfb199 -> f5c71c21). A wiped store holds no `tabhub.browser` and no `tabhub.browserConfigured`, so no explicit choice existed at that moment.
whyItIsConclusive: `currentTabCommandScope` returns undefined without a browser identity, so the relay cannot register a scope at all. Before this change a freshly installed extension therefore could not connect until a human chose a browser.

Both extensions registered within seconds of reinstall (yandex 17:11:01Z, edge 17:11:22Z) and were already labelled correctly, so an identity existed without anyone choosing one. Detection is the only thing that could have supplied it.

The user then opened the extension's options in both and reports the browser shown was already correct. Opening options writes nothing: the save path is bound to the select's `change` event, so looking at a correct value neither creates nor confirms it.
detectionVerification.notCovered: Chrome has not been reloaded and is not connected, so the residue branch — the one that names Chrome by the absence of any other brand — is still unverified on this machine. It is the branch most likely to mislabel, because every Chromium browser that hides its own token falls into it.
detectionVerification.sideEffect: Reinstalling regenerated both installation ids, so both browsers lost their personal-context pairing. Two capability rows are now orphaned: 56024a43 (created 12:28:10Z) and 0bcfb199 (created 16:12:48Z). They can never authenticate again, because no live install presents those ids, and their secrets were only ever held by the erased extension copies.

pairingBannerVerification.method: The user opened the Library in Edge, which was unpaired after the reinstall, and the banner offered pairing without them navigating to a tab drawer. One click produced a capability row for the connected installation 5507a07a-2f23-4174-9428-cd5fbbddd592 and left zero open challenges, so the challenge was created and consumed inside that single action.
pairingBannerVerification.whatItProvesBeyondTheUi: The one-click handover works end to end against the live runtime, and it works the way the security argument in docs/decisions.md claims: the page created a challenge bound to the probed installation and extension origin, handed it over the bridge, and `consumePairingChallenge` accepted it only because the extension presented its own browser-set Origin. No code was displayed and none was typed.
pairingBannerVerification.notYetExercised: `last_used_at` on the new row is still null: a credential that has been issued but not yet spent on a personal-context call. It populates the first time the extension reads or writes context, which is the next step of journey J1.
